newsitem.title: INDIA: India to consider private plans for nuclear power.
newsitem.headline: India to consider private plans for nuclear power.

text.p: India will consider proposals from private investors to set up nuclear power plants on a "case-by-case" basis in the electricity-starved nation, a government statement said on Thursday.

"While the government of India has not invited any offers in the nuclear power sector, it is open to specific offers and will decide its response on a case-by-case basis," Science and Technology Minister Yoginder Alagh said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda earlier this month told a Japanese newspaper that India would allow full foreign ownership of nuclear power plants.
Alagh told the upper house of parliament in a written statement that India allowed 100 percent foreign equity in power sector but "not specifically in the nuclear power sector".
Offers of technical cooperation by private investors would be considered on the basis of "technical suitability, economic attractiveness, environmental and safety considerations," he added.
India has nine nuclear reactors with a total generating capacity of about 2,000 megawatts (MW).
Demand for power is growing at nine percent a year. The country needs to generate 142,000 MW by the year 2007 against current capacity of about 83,288 MW.
India tested a nuclear device in 1974 but says it has no nuclear weapons programme.

Last year, India opposed a global nuclear test ban treaty, saying it would not lead to the elimination of nuclear weapons because it allowed the five acknowledged nuclear powers to continue developing atomic arms through laboratory tests.
The five powers are the United States, Russia, China, France and Britain.
